cases.description: Exact match: request body equals the recorded args exactly. The replayer must return the recorded response with HTTP 200.
Path with a trailing slash must match the same recording as the canonical path without a trailing slash.
cases.notes: The hash key stored in replayerRecordings was computed from the canonical path '/api/scheme/process' (no trailing slash). The replayer must strip the trailing slash before computing the lookup key.

cases.description: Request-scoped tracing headers (x-request-id, x-correlation-id) must be propagated in responses but must NOT affect recording lookup. The same recording is returned regardless of these headers.
cases.notes: The extra headers must not affect lookup. Whether the replayer echoes x-request-id back in the response is implementation-defined and not tested here.

cases.description: A Content-Type header of 'application/json; charset=utf-8' must be treated as equivalent to 'application/json' for body parsing and recording lookup.
cases.notes: Many HTTP clients (Java's HttpURLConnection, Python's requests, .NET's HttpClient) append '; charset=utf-8' by default. Rejecting these as an unknown content-type would break all non-Go conformance clients.

cases.description: JSON object key order in the request body must be ignored. A body with keys in a different order than the canonical form must match the same recording.
cases.notes: The hash in replayerRecordings was computed from stableJson({"input":"MED","schemeId":"ref-scheme-1"}) with keys sorted lexicographically. The request body sends keys in reverse order ({"schemeId":...,"input":...}). After stableJson normalization both produce the same hash. This test catches replayers that hash raw bytes instead of normalized JSON.

cases.description: An array in its recorded order must match the recording.
Reversing array elements must miss the recording for the original order.
A path with different letter case must miss the canonical-path recording.
When no recording matches the (path, body) pair, the replayer must return HTTP 404 with a miss envelope in the shape defined by the 'missEnvelope' section of this corpus.
cases.notes: The 'error' field MUST be the literal string 'no_recording'. The 'bodyHash' MUST equal sha256(stableJson(body)) = sha256('{"input":"UNKNOWN-XYZ"}') = 344956ec... The SDK conformance test harness detects this envelope and fails the test with a clear diagnostic: 'no recording found for path=/api/scheme/process body={...}' rather than a silent subset-match failure.

description: Replayer-contract corpus. Every language SDK's stub HTTP replayer must pass all cases in this file before it is permitted to run engine-slice conformance. Cases cover trailing slashes, path case, extra headers, content-type variants, JSON object-key and array-element ordering, and the miss-envelope shape. A request.rawBody string, when present, is the exact UTF-8 JSON sent on the wire instead of serializing request.body.

lookupAlgorithm.hashInput: Concatenate: normalizedPath, the literal ASCII pipe character '|', then stableJson(body). No separators before or after.
lookupAlgorithm.normalizedPath: Strip one or more trailing slashes from the URL path. Do not lowercase the path: paths are case-sensitive. Example: '/api/scheme/process/' → '/api/scheme/process'.
lookupAlgorithm.stableJson: Recursively sort all JSON object keys in lexicographic order, then serialize as compact JSON (no spaces, no newlines). Arrays are NOT reordered: only object keys are sorted. Example: {"b":2,"a":1} → '{"a":1,"b":2}'.

matchingRules: Trailing slashes on the URL path are ignored: '/api/scheme/process/' matches the same recording as '/api/scheme/process'.
HTTP headers other than Content-Type are ignored for recording lookup. The 'x-request-id', 'x-correlation-id', and similar optional propagation headers MUST NOT change which recording is returned.

The Content-Type request header MUST be treated as 'application/json' when it carries any 'application/json' media type regardless of charset suffix or other parameters. Example: 'application/json; charset=utf-8' is equivalent to 'application/json'.
JSON object key order in the request body MUST be ignored. Two request bodies that are identical after stableJson normalization MUST match the same recording.
Array element order is significant. ["HIGH","MED"] and ["MED","HIGH"] are distinct requests and may match different recordings.
Comparison is performed on the normalized (stableJson) form of the body, NOT on the raw bytes.

missEnvelope.description: When no recording matches the incoming request, the replayer MUST return HTTP 404 with a JSON body that exactly matches this shape. Clients use the 'error' field to detect a miss and fail the conformance test with a clear diagnostic rather than a silent body mismatch.
notes: 'message' is informational only; conformance tests MUST NOT assert on its exact value.
'bodyHash' MUST be sha256(stableJson(body)) as a lowercase hex string.
The Content-Type of the 404 response MUST be 'application/json'.
